text_blocks.snippet: Heart disease is also called cardiovascular disease (CVD). It's a general term encompassing various conditions that affect the heart and blood vessels. While "heart disease" is often used as a simpler term, CVD is the more medically accurate and comprehensive term, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD):
list.snippet: This is the broader term referring to diseases of the heart and blood vessels, including coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, and more.

list.title: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD):
list.snippet: A specific type of heart disease where the arteries supplying blood to the heart muscle narrow, often due to plaque buildup.

list.title: Other Types:
list.snippet: Heart disease also includes conditions like cardiomyopathy (disease of the heart muscle), heart valve disease, and congenital heart defects (present at birth).
